answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a per-identity proof-of-burn escrow: to mint another key an agent must publish a transaction destroying a fixed amount of value, recorded on-chain as a non-redeemable commitment bound to that key. Burned value is never refunded or recycled, so cloning scales linearly in real cost: N identities cost N burns. Validators check the proof from ledger data alone, so a fake timber record or hollow claim fails the first test. Each burn expires like a comet tail, forcing renewal and holding the marginal price per clone above zero: a hard marble floor on an attacker's budget.
